explanation: No actionable defect found in the scoped local-auth fix, approved test corrections, or authentication guide edits; excluded MRU, descriptor-ownership, LCP and PPPoE introduction changes were not judged, and the revised RFC statements match primary RFC 1661 §3.5 and RFC 2865 §§4.1/5. The lost-behavior audit confirms that authlocal/auth.go localAuth.handle preserves credential lookup and PAP/CHAP rejection for authenticated methods, while ppp/session_run.go runNoAuthPhase produces the username-less request now accepted; the existing runAuthPhase required-auth guard precedes that producer, both transport policy handoffs retain AuthRequired = !AllowNoAuth, and startAuthDrain/startPPPoEAuthDrain forward the acceptance to Driver.AuthResponse, so removing the owner-rejected None assertion does not remove mandatory-auth protection. Evidence under plan/verification-evidence/2026-09-22-baseline/ records the username-less regression failing before the fix and authlocal race PASS afterwards, but PPP compilation errors at manager_test.go:357/359 prevented the downgrade regression from executing; subscriber/l2tp-attempt-001 failed admission and attempt-002/native-report.json records proven:true against xl2tpd/pppd on Linux 7.2, with internal/le/deployment/l2tpppp.go L2TPPPP.observe/assertKernelState checking PPP addresses, ping, route withdrawal and teardown—this read-only review ran no validation and claims neither negative-guard execution nor PPPoE/RADIUS interop.
